title: History of p5.js and Creative Coding
description: An interactive timeline tracing the evolution of creative coding tools from Design By Numbers at MIT Media Lab to the modern p5.js library.
subject: Mathematics
topic: History of p5.js and Creative Coding
author: Dan McCreary
learningObjectives: Sequence the lineage of creative coding tools from Design By Numbers (1996-1999) through Processing (2001) and Processing.js (2008) to p5.js (2013)
Identify the people behind each milestone, including John Maeda, Ben Fry and Casey Reas, John Resig, and Lauren McCarthy
Explain how web standards such as HTML5 Canvas, WebGL, Web Audio, and getUserMedia made a browser-native p5.js possible
Compare the five event categories (Processing, p5.js, Web Standards, Related Projects, Organizations) using the timeline filter buttons
Analyze why the shift from Java-based Processing to JavaScript-based p5.js broadened access to creative coding
